protocol.description:
A client asks for glass under parts of its surfaces: rounded rectangles where the compositor blurs and tints what is below the surface by then and bends it at the edge, the glass resc-desk draws under its own panels and windows.
Panels are drawn in the order given, each right before the surface's own content and over every panel given before it: a panel blurs the panels under it. Content of the same surface does not come between two of its panels; for glass over content (a menu's glass over a list) put the upper panel on a subsurface above it: the compositor draws surfaces bottom to top and each surface's glass blurs everything drawn below it, subsurfaces and their glass included, so windows in windows in windows nest.
The surface should be see-through (an alpha format, premultiplied) where its glass is meant to show.

request.name: get_glass
request.description: One per surface; a second one while the first lives is a protocol error.

interface.name: resc_glass_v1
interface.description: State is double-buffered: the panels given since the surface's last commit replace its panels on its next commit; a commit with none given keeps the panels it has.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The surface's panels go with its next commit.

request.name: clear
request.description: The surface has no panels from its next commit on (until some are added).

request.name: add_panel
request.description:
A panel at (x, y) of size width × height in surface-local coordinates, with corners of radius `r_tl`, `r_tr`, `r_br`, `r_bl` (top left, then clockwise). `blur`: the frost's gaussian sigma in surface-local px, 0 for clear glass, negative for the desk's own (as on its windows). `tint`: 0xAARRGGBB, straight alpha, laid over the frost; 0 for the desk's window tint. `bezel`: the band along the edge where the glass bends what is under it, surface px, negative for the desk's own. At most 64 panels per surface.
What the user set for the program in the desk's settings goes over what it asks for: blur, bezel and the tint's alpha as much stronger or weaker as those are than the desk's default.

request.name: clip_panel

description.summary: the last panel cut to a rectangle

request.description: The panel added last shows only inside this rectangle (surface-local): a card scrolled half out of a list's view. Without a panel added since the last clear or commit it does nothing.

entry.name: panel
entry.summary: the look of the desk's panels: a soft shadow, a hairline rim, an inset highlight
